title: phpdup configuration
description: Schema for phpdup.json. The phpdup CLI runs equivalent checks at load time via Phpdup\Cli\ConfigLoader::validate() and surfaces field-path errors before any analysis begins. Defaults below match Phpdup\Cli\Config.

paths.description: Source roots to scan. When this key is absent, the scan roots must come from the CLI args. An explicit empty list is refused at load (exit 2, "paths must not be empty") — the loader never falls through to argv for a present-but-empty paths key, hence minItems:1. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (the scan roots are fixed before discovery walks the tree; at the root layer the key still replaces the CLI arguments when both are present, and that replacement is now surfaced as a phpdup: warning: load note — the silent clobber it used to be was the once-077 complaint) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

exclude.description: Glob patterns excluded from the scan. ** matches recursively.

exclude_reset.description: Opt-out of the item-5.2 append-merge for exclude lists. Excludes normally STACK across defaults -> profile -> root config -> CLI dict -> per-directory layers (deduped); "exclude_reset": true discards every INHERITED layer below the resetting one (stock defaults AND profile) so only the config-file/dict lists survive. Also honored per-directory: a .phpdup.json carrying it resets the inherited chain for that subtree at scan time (once-S28), and the --auto-tune probe counts the tree with it applied. Shape-checked boolean — any non-boolean value exits 2. CLI: none (config-file family key).

min_block_size.description: Minimum AST node count for a block to be considered. Must be <= max_block_size; the cross-field check is enforced at load time. Also honored per-subtree (a .phpdup.json gates extraction for its subtree — top-level blocks stay exempt, engine-057).

max_block_size.description: Maximum AST node count for a block. Must be >= min_block_size. Blocks above this are dropped before fingerprinting. Also honored per-subtree via a per-directory .phpdup.json.

normalization_mode.description: strict = variable-rename tolerant only. default = also collapse literal values. aggressive = also collapse method, property, and class names. Also honored per-subtree via a per-directory .phpdup.json (the mode rides the worker tooling and IndexStore cache keys, so a subtree may normalize differently without poisoning the rest).

normalization.description: Normalization post-pass plugins (root-config object; the only admitted sub-key is plugins — any other sub-key fails the load as an unknown config key). ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (plugin lists ride the worker tooling and cache keys from the ROOT roster only) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

plugins.description: Class names implementing Phpdup\Normalization\NormalizationPlugin, loaded by name and run by PluginRegistry as a post-pass inside the Normalizer (PreprocessWorker::toolFor() AND the per-file IndexStore cache key both fold this list in, so adding, removing or reordering a plugin invalidates the warm caches rather than replaying stale streams). An empty or absent list is the stock behavior. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying the normalization key fails the load (once-S67 flipped the old silent-ignore into a loud refusal — the roster above is root-only by construction); the key is also absent from the CLI roster.

similarity_threshold.description: Jaccard threshold for the near-duplicate clustering phase. Below this, the type-3 containment fallback may still apply when optional_blocks.enabled is true. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (Jaccard scores whole clusters, which span directories; every reader receives the ROOT config, so the per-directory value was moved and never observed) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

tree_threshold.description: APTED tree-edit-distance similarity threshold applied to candidates that passed the Jaccard filter. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (a pair spans two directories — the same ambiguity law as max_ted_size) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

min_cluster_impact.description: Minimum cluster impact (approximately the count of duplicated lines) required for a cluster to appear in the report. Quiets output without changing clustering. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (the impact floor measures whole clusters, which span directories) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

max_df.description: Maximum document-frequency for an n-gram before it is treated as boilerplate and dropped from candidate-pair generation. 0.01 suits real codebases; bump to ~0.5 for tiny fixtures where every n-gram is 'common' by ratio. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (the boilerplate floor prunes the shared candidate index once per run) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

candidate_budget.description: Safety cap on candidate pairs emitted during clustering. A pathological clone family halts loudly instead of exhausting memory. 0 = unlimited (opts out of the guard). Default 60,000,000; CLI: --candidate-budget. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (the memory guard protects the one clustering pass; it reads the root config) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

ngram_size.description: Token-level n-gram length used for fingerprinting and Jaccard similarity. Also honored per-subtree: a .phpdup.json carrying it changes the bag for that subtree (the value rides the worker tooling and IndexStore cache keys).

fingerprint_id_mode.description: Identifier-numbering form of the similarity fingerprints. 'numbered' = legacy: the aggressive Normalizer's first-occurrence counters (__V3, __CALL12, __PROP0, __CLASS7) ride into the n-gram bag and the tree-edit labels, so one inserted guard renumbers every later identifier and breaks the fingerprint for the rest of the block. 'un-numbered' = strip the counters from bag tokens AND TED labels in lockstep (Phpdup\Util\IdentifierIds); multiset Jaccard, containment and TED similarity are monotone under this coarsening, so no edge accepted today is lost and guard-drift clones finally link. Structural hashes, anti-unification and ML pair features keep numbered input either way. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (mixed modes would poison the shared candidate index and warm caches). No CLI flag in v1. The mode value rides the worker tooling key, the per-file index cache key and the cluster-cache config key; 'numbered' keeps every cache and golden byte-identical.

max_ted_size.description: Node-count cap for APTED tree-edit judgment. A candidate pair whose LARGER member exceeds this cap skips the TED call entirely: it is accepted on Jaccard alone with edge tier 'jaccard-unverified' (weight = the Jaccard score), or falls through to the containment/IR/ML tiers unchanged — APTED is the quadratic-cost site (the historical figure quoted in pre-2026-11 prose, 161s / 1.2GB on a 1000-node pair, predates the engine-S09 banded DP + memoisation rewrite; post-S09 cap-size near-identical pairs measure in seconds, and the DP space is banded). Default 800 equals the max_block_size extraction ceiling, so no real block can exceed it and the gate is inert out of the box: every existing verdict, cache and golden stays byte-identical. Lower it (e.g. 200-400) on giant-clone corpora to trade exactness for wall time. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — a pair spans two directories, so a per-directory cap would be ambiguous. No CLI flag in v1. The cap rides the cluster-cache config key and is applied identically by the serial Clusterer and the parallel PairScoreWorker. A separate AGGREGATE guard (Clusterer::DEFAULT_MAX_TED_COST = 100,000,000 node-pair units, an internal constant — not this key) charges every verdict the SERIAL engine pays and halts loudly before crossing; the fork lane has no aggregate counterpart yet (docs/adr/0003, cost-ceilings section).

window_oversized.description: Item 1.2 (E2): extraction posture for blocks ABOVE max_block_size. Default true: an oversized body is never silently invisible — the extractor cuts maximal contiguous statement windows (each capped at max_block_size nodes) out of it, and those windows fingerprint and cluster like any other block. Windows carry the synthetic 'window' kind: AST-addressing surfaces (--apply, refactor patches, loader relocation) refuse them loudly, mirroring the 'script' fold precedent. Counting honesty (item 0.6) at the granularity that stayed invisible: a parent from which NOTHING survives (zero windows, or a kind with no statement list) counts once in summary.blocks_oversized, while statements a SALVAGED parent's packing silently gave up on (invalid line-geometry, sub-floor remainders) count individually; the disclosed lone-giant residual stays invisible to v1 windowing. This default-ON posture is an owner-ratified behavior change (exec order 2026-11-28): corpora that DO contain oversized declarations report differently than before item 1.2 (new window species mean new clusters) — the improve_logic_info.md §8.4 default-off re-run rule predates the window mechanism (it described the max_ted_size-only v1 cure) and does not imply doc-continuity here. Corpora without oversized blocks keep every report byte-identical. Set false for the historical posture: oversized blocks are dropped and only the counter is printed. Deliberately NO CLI flag (config-only extraction stance, max_ted_size precedent). ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — the posture is bound into the extraction and cluster cache keys, so a per-directory split would forge two identities for one run.

honor_gitignore.description: Item 5.2 .gitignore leg (W2a): respect .gitignore files while scanning — the scan-root file plus every nested one the descent reaches. Dialect per gitignore(5): within one file the LAST matching line wins (negation ! included); across files the DEEPEST file that answers decides; trailing / marks directory-only rules; a leading / — or any interior slash — anchors the pattern to the ignore file own directory, slash-free patterns match the entry last path segment at any depth. Bracket classes ([abc], [!abc], ranges, byte semantics) and backslash escapes compile through the same bounded glob + automaton engine that guards the exclude lists (once-095 posture): over-budget ignore files (size or line cap) fail CLOSED to a single * exclusion with a visible note, and cache bounds (per-file honor cap, miss-cache cap) fail OPEN once with a visible note. The two channels never override each other: an exclude-list pruned directory is never revived by a negation, and a .gitignore below an excluded directory is never read (git own documented limitation, mirrored deliberately). .git/info/exclude and core.excludesFile are out of scope (the doc letter names .gitignore files), as is walking above the scan root — run phpdup at the root whose ignores you mean to honor. Honest accounting without per-path noise: each drained root adds one aggregate gitignore: N paths excluded line to the scan-notes channel; no JSON summary key changes. Bound into the extraction and cluster cache keys (allowedKinds/window_oversized doctrine): flipping the flag invalidates existing caches once, clean misses into fresh saves, no PARSER_VERSION bump. Default false keeps every historical walk byte-identical. CLI: --honor-gitignore. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — file membership is a whole-run stance; one cache identity per run.

idiom_mining.description: Item 3.1 ingestion (MINE-D): the idiom-census demand knob. True: preprocessing arms the subtree census miner on the SAME statement-list walker the fragment engine uses (one traversal, §5c) — frequent concrete subtrees (6-40 nodes) are mined from every parsed file, ingested per file into the run's SequenceIndex, and the JSON report gains the conditional trailing `summary.idiom_census` block: corpus hash/site totals plus the top-50 maximal idiom rows in deterministic order (nested families suppressed), locations materialised only for hashes seen at 2+ sites per the substrate's two-pass memory policy. PRECONDITION: `kinds` must explicitly include 'fragment' — the miner rides the fragment-gated statement-list capture and the empty all-default roster deliberately excludes fragment; an armed load without it fails the Config construction invariant at once (exit 2) rather than reporting a quiet zero census. An armed run reprocesses every file: cache reuse is disabled because warm-reused files emit no mined rows, and a census missing its reused files would present a partial truth as complete. The key is bound into the extraction cache key as the prophylactic second belt (flip invalidates warm caches once; no PARSER_VERSION bump). Census feeds NOTHING into clustering: cluster output for a given roster is identical armed or unarmed — only the trailing summary block differs, so frozen payloads (goldens) are untouched by the unarmed default. Deliberately NO CLI flag at this tip (the Command option roster rides a later train; ml_pair_allow_private staging precedent) — the knob speaks through phpdup.json. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — one census per run, never one per subtree.

symbols_forced.description: Item 3.4 (S4): the duplicate-symbol demand knob. True: the cluster stage builds a SymbolIndex over the final block index (master-side only — the construction reads data already resident, no new field crosses the worker wire) and injects its forced candidate pairs AHEAD of the natural stream: blocks sharing a case-folded function/method name across owners (file+class), twin class short names with a different qualified class (the single route magic __* names may use — diverged twin constructors), and named blocks from files sharing a basename across paths (the same-filename-different-logic archetype, S1-46). Forced pairs bypass the bag and df PREFILTERS (inverted index, max_df, the F3 mass bound, fragment suppression — they never enter through those doors) but NOT the scoring: every forced pair rides the regular scoring lanes at its real similarity. An above-floor pair merges like any edge (its cluster gains a symbol-pair-merged note); a below-floor pair never merges and surfaces as a symbol-pair-shadow architectural finding carrying the measured jaccard, containment and size ratio — evidence, not a cluster. Magic names, same-owner groups, and groups over the determinism ceilings (12 distinct sites, 32 pooled blocks; over-cap groups drop whole, never sliced) never force. Findings ride the existing architectural_findings cluster surface: the JSON payload gains zero new keys. Unclustered-orphan residual (both endpoints singleton, below every floor) has no carrier in the cluster-bound spine and rides only the candidate counters — row-level surfacing is a payload-shape change owned by the schema window, disclosed in the S4 lane report. Bound into the cluster cache key (arm flips invalidate warm .cluster stores once; no PARSER_VERSION bump). CLI: --symbols. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — one forced-symbol enumeration per run; pairs span directories (candidate_mass_filter / idiom_mining class).

helper_adoption.description: Item 3.2 adoption (MINE-D-2): the helper re-implementation demand knob. True: once blocks exist, preprocessing derives a HelperAdoption ledger over the SAME armed idiom substrate 3.1 mined — each small named function/method (at most 5 top-level statements) contributes its in-body maximal census patterns as wildcard-keyed lookups (the fold keys already abstract literals and renumber parameter slots), and every other occurrence of the same pattern is accounted as an inline re-implementing copy (per-file counts + canonical 'file:line' samples). The acceptance pair: with idiom_mining on over tests/Fixtures/micro-fixture, MicroFixtureEnv::isDev and MicroFixtureEnv::baseUrl each report 5 inline copies in the five inline_*.php files. PRECONDITION: `idiom_mining` must be true — adoption re-queries the mined census (the §5c one-shared-miner law mints no second walker and no second lookup index); an armed load without it fails the Config construction invariant (exit 2), mirroring the idiom roster precondition. The knob crosses NO worker wire and persists NOTHING: mined rows, payloads and the IndexStore config key are byte-identical armed or not (the summary is rebuilt in-process every run from census + blocks), which is why — unlike idiom_mining — this key deliberately does NOT join the cache-key roster; a proof test pins the key's invariance across the flip. Default-off keeps every historical run byte-identical; the ledger is reached today through the pipeline API (sequenceIndex->helperAdoption()), the JSON summary surface of the same train as idiom_census rides a later reporting leg (recorded follow-on, MINE-D.r1 §4 conditional-key precedent: no schema bump). Deliberately NO CLI flag at this tip (idiom_mining/ml_pair_allow_private staging posture) — the knob speaks through phpdup.json. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — one adoption ledger per run, never one per subtree.

history.description: Item 4.2 (git-history correlation): arm the blame/log sidecar. True: after clustering, every cross-file cluster is correlated against git history — one `git blame --porcelain` per member file (parsed once into line->(sha,time,msg), cached under cache_dir/history/ keyed by repo@HEAD+file) plus ONE `git log -M --name-only --since` per repo give per-member last-changed dates, which members changed ALONE inside the window, whether a lone commit message matches fix|security|bug, and same-commit co-change counts (rename-aware both legs: log -M lists rename commits under the new path, blame previous headers supply the old names). The JSON summary gains the conditional trailing `summary.cluster_history` block (JsonSchemaSpec::summaryShape(historyArmed: true) / historyBlockShape(); demand-armed keys ride schema 1.8 with the armed shape spelled — NO SCHEMA_VERSION change, the unarmed payload stays byte-identical) and a lone fix raises a WARNING finding (code history-lone-fix; notes for plain divergence), corroborating item 4.1 drift findings where both fire. At most 100 rows print in `summary.cluster_history` (the `omitted` counter reports the rest); the cap is presentation-only — findings for capped-out clusters still surface. Correlation feeds NOTHING into clustering: cluster bytes never move armed or unarmed — only the sidecar block and the appended findings differ. Fails open everywhere: missing git binary, non-repo targets, untracked files, corrupt histories and 15s command timeouts all answer verdict unmeasurable with an aggregate scan note — never a fatal, never an exit-code change. Cache law (§8.4): opt-in features zero churn — the history cache lives under its own cache_dir/history/ subtree, never bound into extraction/cluster cache keys (a flip changes no similarity bytes). CLI: --history. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — history answers a whole report, a subtree flip would mint a half-armed census.

history_window_months.description: Item 4.2: the 'last N months' window for lone-change and activity claims (improve_logic.md 4.2: 'members changed alone in the last N months'). Snapped to a UTC day boundary per run so the git --since argument and the cache_dir/history/log key are stable for the calendar day. Must be >= 1: a zero or negative window would gate every history verdict to nothing. Deliberately NO CLI flag (numeric report-tuning knob, max_ted_size precedent — --history arms, this key tunes). Only meaningful with history: true. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (same posture as history).

call_sequence.description: Item 3.5 call-sequence idioms (MINE-E): the ordered-callee demand knob. True: preprocessing extends the SAME fragment-gated statement-list walker §5c licenses (one traversal, no second pass) with a 'calls' flavor — every function/method/closure body captures its ORDERED callee-name sequence (CallGraph::nameOf semantics: method calls receiver-blind bare names, static calls 'Class::method', functions their written name; dynamic names dropped), then mines sliding windows of length 2-4 shared by at least 2 sites with differing literals and constant arguments abstracted into per-slot value tables — a cURL bootstrap or an ssh2 login sequence collapses to ONE protocol row and its arg-diff table carries the evidence (the doc's archetype: CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER => false x2 / true x1 across the bootstraps). PRECONDITION: `idiom_mining` must be true — the miner rides the fragment-gated capture and the same armed-census door; an armed load without it fails the Config construction invariant (exit 2), mirroring the helper_adoption precondition exactly. Like idiom_mining an armed run reprocesses every file (warm reuse emits no rows — a census missing them would present partial truth) and the key binds into the extraction cache key as the prophylactic second belt (flip invalidates warm caches once; no PARSER_VERSION bump). The JSON report gains the conditional trailing `summary.call_sequences` block (JsonSchemaSpec::summaryShape(callsArmed: true) / callBlockShape(); demand-armed keys ride schema 1.8 with the armed shape spelled — NO SCHEMA_VERSION change, the unarmed payload stays byte-identical, goldens frozen): corpus window/site counters plus the top-50 maximal protocol rows in deterministic sites/files/name order (nested windows suppressed via the census's own edge map), canonical 'file:line' samples, and per-slot differing-constant tables whose value counters are corpus-complete (cap 8 values per slot; slots with one distinct value and no hole are not tabled). The census feeds NOTHING into clustering or scoring — no MatchTier is minted (the dual-vocabulary law is untouched); sequence evidence stays a census ledger like idioms. When `helper_adoption` is armed too, adoption rows gain `callers` counts through a receiver-blind name join over this same mined census (occurrences inside the helper's own definition span excluded; per-name location overflow counted — the honest worst direction). Deliberately NO CLI flag at this tip (idiom_mining/ml_pair_allow_private staging posture) — the knob speaks through phpdup.json. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — one call census per run, never one per subtree.

literal_census.description: Item 3.3 repeated-literal census (MINE-E): the literals / class-constants / enum-cases demand knob. True: preprocessing reads each file's RAW parsed tree (the same single walk; normalization erases literals downstream, so the census must read raw — done in-worker where the tree is already resident) and counts five buckets: `string` values >= 12 bytes (URLs, SQL fragments, messages; heredoc/nowdoc included), `array` literals with >= 3 entries hashed ORDER-INSENSITIVELY (status maps, allow-lists, option tables match across entry shuffles; spread entries become value holes), `number` constants grouped by value plus syntactic position (trivial 0/1/-1 and array-entry values skipped, so the doc's '86400 on 112 lines' archetype surfaces at its call sites), `skeleton` interpolated strings grouped by literal skeleton with recognized SQL folded to verb+table via SqlTableExtractor (repeated query shapes count as one entry; concatenation-built SQL is NOT captured — disclosed follow-on), and `const` — class-constant declarations, enum cases and every class-const FETCH grouped by NAME alone, so five STATUS_MAP copies across five classes land in one row with decl/enum_case/use role counters. Near-duplicate strings additionally union into edit-distance families within length bands (drifting allow-lists read as one family with joined sites/files); a corpus over 400 distinct strings skips family computation honestly (families_computed: false). No precondition and no fragment roster (it walks the whole tree, not list capture) — but like idiom_mining the knob MINTS per-file rows, so an armed run bypasses the IndexStore entirely and the key binds into the extraction cache key (flip invalidates warm caches once; no PARSER_VERSION bump). The JSON report gains the conditional trailing `summary.literal_census` block (JsonSchemaSpec::summaryShape(literalsArmed: true) / literalBlockShape(); rides schema 1.8, NO SCHEMA_VERSION change — the unarmed payload is byte-identical, goldens frozen): per-bucket entry/site totals (counted at every support level), the top-50 rows needing >= 2 sites (numbers >= 2 files) in kind/sites/files/hash order with roles and canonical samples, and the family list. The census feeds NOTHING into clustering — literals and constants stay invisible to cluster membership exactly as before; only the trailing summary block moves. Deliberately NO CLI flag at this tip (idiom_mining staging posture) — the knob speaks through phpdup.json. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — one literal census per run, never one per subtree.

corpus_rollups.description: Item 2.2 (ROLLUP): the corpus-awareness demand knob. True: the report stage runs RollupAnalyzer over the FULL ranked cluster set plus the retained blocks and scanned files — per-file comparable-line/declaration/expression/call-site/SQL-table tallies (call sites follow the CallGraph kind set: function, method and static calls; property reads are not calls), both-direction twin FILE pairs (each direction's linked coverage >= 0.5; demoted clusters exempt from the numerators per the 2.4 doctrine), a seed-direct leg comparing same-relative-path and same-basename pairs even when clustering never linked them, declared-only rows for seed pairs one side of which emitted no blocks, and mirrored DIRECTORY pair groups. The JSON report gains the conditional trailing `summary.rollups` block: corpus-complete totals plus presentation-capped top_files / twin_pairs / mirrored_directories / declared_only_pairs rows with sibling *_truncated counters (the idiom_census/counters-corpus-complete-presentation-capped posture); the CLI gains one compact rollups trailer line. Rollups feed NOTHING into clustering: cluster output is identical armed or unarmed — only the trailing summary block and the trailer line differ, so frozen payloads (goldens) are untouched by the unarmed default and no schema version event rides the key (conditional-key carve-out). Report-stage recompute only: nothing persists, no cache key binds this knob (unlike idiom_mining's extraction-key prophylactic — the pass reads only state the run already carries). A non-boolean fails the load. Deliberately NO CLI flag at this tip (the Command option roster rides a later train; ml_pair_allow_private/idiom_mining staging precedent) — the knob speaks through phpdup.json. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — one rollup census per run, never one per subtree.

themes.description: Item 6.4 (THEME): the finding-theming demand knob. True: the report stage runs ThemeAnalyzer over the REPORTED findings — each cluster's signature is its shared callee vocabulary (a span-scoped read of the item-3.5 call-sequence census name index, no second mining pass; degrades honestly to pattern tags alone when call_sequence is unarmed, disclosed in basis.call_census) plus its member directories — and seeds appearing in >= 2 clusters greedily claim findings into themes: vocabulary seeds first (the letter's primary grouping axis), then directory seeds for the remainder, coverage desc / seed asc ordering with the FindingId tie-break, one theme per cluster. The JSON report gains the conditional trailing `summary.themes` block (JsonSchemaSpec::summaryShape(themes: true) / themeBlockShape()): basis + corpus-complete totals (including the honest themeless_clusters residual) + presentation-capped theme rows (content-derived id, kind, seed, heuristic label 'seed › dominant_dir', measured cluster count and line sum, bounded dirs/vocabulary/cluster_ids samples with truncation counters). The roll-up is JSON-summary-only: unlike the corpus_rollups precedent the CLI gains no trailer line, and the TUI and server surfaces are unaffected. Semantic labels ('outbound HTTP' as a phrase) are shipped by the `phpdup audit` theme-merge pass (item 8.2 — its LLM layer labels the groups the heuristic seeds found); this heuristic block keeps its label-free 'seed › dominant_dir' naming by design, and the two surfaces never overwrite each other. Theming feeds NOTHING into clustering or other findings: armed and unarmed cluster output is identical; no cache key binds the knob (pure report-stage view over state the run already carries); the unarmed payload is byte-identical so no SCHEMA_VERSION event rides the key (the idiom_census/corpus_rollups conditional-key carve-out). A non-boolean fails the load. Deliberately NO CLI flag at this tip (corpus_rollups staging precedent) — the knob speaks through phpdup.json. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — themes group the whole summary, never one subtree at a time.

candidate_mass_filter.description: Item 0.5 (F3): the multiset upper-bound pre-test inside candidate generation. Sum_v min(A(v),B(v)) over the ngram bags upper-bounds the true intersection, so a pair whose bound (plus df-cap skipped-mass slack) cannot reach the Jaccard or containment threshold is skipped WITHOUT the intersection scoring walk — measured 42-46x fewer pairs enumerated on the storm corpora with zero true-edge loss (improve_logic_info.md section 3). Default true; set false to restore the pre-F3 enumeration byte-for-byte. Deliberately NO CLI flag (engine-consistency stance, max_ted_size precedent). ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (a candidate pair spans two directories; the one shared enumeration stream takes one stance).

ted_weights.description: Edit-cost model for the APTED tree-edit-distance tier (Phpdup\Similarity\EditCostModel). 'default' = uniform cost 1.0 per node insert/delete/substitute — the model every historical similarity, cache and golden byte was produced with. 'semantic' = a node-kind weight table (method calls and control flow cost more than literals), honored identically by the serial Clusterer and the parallel PairScoreWorker — one admission feeds both scorers. Admitted as a plain enum at validate() time: an unknown value exits 2 ("ted_weights must be one of default|semantic"). ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (once-S67: the loud refusal replaces the old silent ignore — pair-scoring stance is chosen once per run). The value rides the cluster-cache config key, so switching models replays as a cache MISS rather than mixing cost models inside one cache. CLI: --ted-weights.

max_hole_coverage.description: Hole-coverage ceiling for extraction honesty. Every cluster's generalized template is measured (hole_coverage = fraction of its AST units inside hole subtrees); a cluster whose coverage is STRICTLY ABOVE this threshold is marked re_expressed in the JSON and CLI reports, and its longest hole-free top-level statement run is surfaced as hole_fragment — the part actually worth extracting. Default 1.0 disables the rule (coverage can never exceed it), so every existing report and golden stays byte-identical. Lower it (e.g. 0.4) to flag hole-riddled abstractions — annotation never deletion: phpdup does not drop evidence based on a threshold. CLI: --max-hole-coverage. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — a cluster spans directories, and the threshold is a stance about the one final report.

cache_dir.description: Directory used for the AST cache and per-file index snapshots. The default is RELATIVE, so a normal run stores blobs inside the scanned tree; when that is the case phpdup refuses to read the cache unless you pass the CLI-only --trust-in-root-cache flag (engine-006: a committed cache in a cloned repo could be a planted decoy). Point cache_dir outside the tree (e.g. a shared temp dir) to keep reads trusted without the flag. CLI: --trust-in-root-cache (no config-file key; there is no 'trust_in_root_cache' setting here by design — the opt-in must be explicit per invocation). ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (one cache root per run; a subtree choosing it is inert (its reader receives the root config)) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

parallelism.description: Declared posture for parallel stages: one of auto, off, manual. ADMITTED, ENUM-VALIDATED AND CARRIED THROUGH THE CONFIG LAYERS — BUT NOT READ BY ANY RUNTIME DECISION TODAY: the effective controls are `workers` (0 = auto-detect, 1 = serial) and pcntl availability in WorkerPool. Setting this key changes nothing observable; it rides the withOverrides layer only (php-dup-finder-once-078 doc-truth wave, 2026-11: documented inert until a wire-or-retire ruling lands, the sibling story of optional_blocks.min_segment_length). ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (pool posture is chosen once per run) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

workers.description: Worker count for parallel preprocess + pair scoring. 0 = auto-detect from nproc / /proc/cpuinfo. 1 = serial. Higher is explicit. Values above the pool ceiling (4 x detected CPUs, WorkerPool::workersCeiling()) are admitted, NOT rejected: the run exits 0 with a `phpdup: warning:` load note and WorkerPool::clampWorkers bounds every actual fork set at the ceiling (shell-S10, shell-038 — the fork-storm fix chose clamp-and-warn over validation because an oversized count is a stance, not a shape error). CLI: -j/--workers. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (the pool is minted from the root config once per run) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

incremental.description: Reuse per-file block snapshots from the IndexStore when the source hash, parser version, and config key all match. Disable for benchmarks or paranoid runs. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (the reuse policy is the run's cache posture, read from the root config) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

lazy_ast.description: Drop each block's original AST after fingerprinting; reload on demand inside the anti-unifier via BlockAstLoader. Disable for max speed when RAM is plentiful. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (the AST loader is minted from the ROOT flag alone (RefactorStage), so a per-directory true would unload ASTs the run could never reload) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

kinds.description: Block kinds to extract. Empty list (or omitted) means accept all twelve traversable kinds — the item-1.3 'script' kind (folds of top-level statements: requires, guards, bootstrap runs outside any function) and the item-2.1 'fragment' kind (contiguous 3..40-statement runs mined from every executable statement list: function/method/closure bodies, loop and branch bodies, and the script fold's top-level buckets) are NEVER part of the implicit set and must be named explicitly. Script and fragment clusters are detection-only in v1: --apply and --refactor-patch refuse them (typed exit 1); text rendering (--patch/--diff) stays allowed. The item-2.3 'class' kind (named class/interface/trait/enum declarations fingerprinted by their member skeleton — the name-blanked declaration tree, so same-shape-different-name pairs cluster) is the third never-implicit kind: it surfaces the doc's declaration twins (shape_exact) and skeleton families (a class_shape table per class cluster: per shared method, distinct strict/fold hash counts and the verdict identical-in-all | parameterizable | divergent = the base-class proposal). Class clusters are likewise detection-only in v1 (apply/patch refused, typed exit 1; the class_shape key is conditional and appears only under this posture, so default-run JSON keeps its frozen shape). The item-7.2b 'html_script' kind — the fourth never-implicit kind — folds inline <script> content windows of templates: the fold carries the FULL mixed sequence (raw-HTML runs as position-marked sentinel members, real PHP statements between ?> and <?php escapes ride as real Nodes; language='text/babel' variants are ordinary raw-text windows), and raw text hashes as raw text, so identical JS clusters across HTML chrome variance — the item's whole point. External src= scripts mint no window (no inline content) and unclosed windows are discarded (v1 law). html_script clusters are likewise detection-only in v1 (apply/patch refused, typed exit 1) — with one honest departure from the three synthetic siblings: the loader RE-DERIVES a fold positionally from the file's raw bytes (lineage-pinned), so signature and reporting surfaces keep working after lazy_ast unloads them. The item-7.1 'text' kind is the fifth never-implicit kind and the only one that widens the SCANNER: non-PHP files (.js/.mjs/.ts/.jsx/.json/.tpl/.twig/.yaml/.yml/.sh/.css/.html per the profile roster) are lexed loosely, identifiers/numbers/strings blanked, and k-token windows shared across files extended to maximal runs — each run a Block(kind:'text') whose payload is the blanked token fold (raw file bytes never enter the fold). Type-1/type-2 only, per the doc: renamed JS twins, template twins and copied workflow YAML fuse in the exact-hash tier (identical blanked runs share one structuralHash), near-runs ride the shared-bag jaccard tier. Text clusters are detection evidence only: --apply/--refactor-patch refuse them (typed exit 1; folds carry no PHP), text rendering (--patch/--diff) stays allowed, and the loader refuses to 're-derive' one (there is no PHP parse behind it). Because the tier arms the scan run-wide, 'text' must be named in the ROOT roster (config or --kinds); a per-directory .phpdup.json naming it is refused loudly. Empty list still means the twelve traversable PHP kinds. Equivalent to --kinds on the CLI. Also honored per-subtree: a .phpdup.json restricting kinds gates that subtree's extraction.

sort.description: Cluster sort spec — KEY[:DIRECTION]. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (ordering is a stance about the one final report; the old per-directory admission was inert (reader: ReportStage, root config only)) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells). Keys: impact, members, block-size, lines, similarity, confidence, name, file, id. Aliases: size/count → members; block_size → block-size. Direction defaults to desc; a leading '-' forces desc, '+' forces asc. Equivalent to --sort on the CLI.

scope.description: Repo scope filter for reported clusters. 'all' = no filtering (legacy behaviour). 'single' = keep clusters whose members share one repo; 'multi' = keep clusters spanning >=2 distinct non-empty member repo labels; the item-5.1 ladder words 'intra-file' | 'intra-package' | 'cross-package' | 'cross-repo' filter on the coarsest true rung (cross-repo is the spelled form of multi) and are closed-set values checked before the label branch, so a scan root literally named 'cross-repo' cannot shadow the word; any other non-empty string = keep clusters with at least one member carrying that exact repo label. Repo labels resolve per file by walking up to and including the longest matching scan root for a .git directory-or-file marker (nearest in-boundary repo; markers ABOVE a root are operator layout and ignored), falling back to the root basename — the identical word pre-5.1 runs printed. Applied after ranking: --limit/--sort and the CI gates all measure the filtered slice. Armed scope also auto-demotes vendored duplicates (item 5.2): clusters whose every member file is a third-party copy — a nested vendor/ dir, a package-named dir declared by a scan root's composer.lock, or a known upstream header — leave the reported slice and the CI gates into the report's own conditional summary.vendored_duplicates section (one stderr line names the demotion; mixed first-party/vendored clusters stay — vendored↔vendored is the exact pair rule). Detection is always-on but inert to default output; the key opens only on scope-armed runs, schema 1.8 rides unchanged (conditional-key posture). Cross-repo analysis means one scan path per repository. CLI: --scope. Root-config/CLI only; a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (report-level stance, chosen once per run).

scope_labels.description: Item 5.1 (scope-counts leg): the repo/package ladder demand knob. True: ReportStage counts the four-rung ladder (intra-file / intra-package / cross-package / cross-repo) over the REPORTED cluster set via ClusterScope::counts() and the JSON payload grows the conditional trailing summary.scope_counts block (one int per ladder word, sum identity with summary.clusters — structural), each cluster a scope_ladder word, each member a package key (the composer name of the nearest composer.json at or below the file's scan root, charset-guarded and degrading to the repo label — an unreadable or corrupt manifest fails open with one skip-with-note per directory on the scan-notes channel, never a fatal); the CLI trailer gains one compact scope-labels line. Labels ride Block fields stamped every run from the current roots (the RepoLabels restamp law: run context, never persisted, never trusted from a cache — which is why, like corpus_rollups, nothing here binds a cache key and no PARSER_VERSION bump was owed). Unlabeled members join no second bucket: a fully-unlabeled multi-file cluster reads intra-package, never a speculative cross-*. Unarmed (default): nothing computes, no key opens, every payload byte-identical and the goldens frozen (demand-armed conditional keys ride schema 1.8, NO SCHEMA_VERSION change — the idiom_census/vendored_duplicates/corpus_rollups carve-out, MINE-D section 4). The cross-repo audit scoring leg of item 5.1 is the separate score_mode knob ('typed'), not this one. CLI: --scope-labels. A non-boolean fails the load. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — one scope census per run, never one per subtree.

score_mode.description: Scoring stance for cross-repo clones. 'global' = legacy math, byte-identical to every historical score, baseline and gate run. 'per-repo' = the >3-namespaces penalty in confidence (Ranker) and safety (SafetyScorer) is evaluated on the namespace spread within the densest member repo, so a subsystem mirrored across packages is no longer double-penalized for its mirroring (quantified: 13.2% of phlix clusters took the paired −0.05/−0.10 hit). 'typed' = audit posture: cross-repo clusters skip that penalty and instead gain +0.05 confidence / +0.10 safety — one shared helper erases N repo-local copies, so the spread is evidence FOR the refactor. Single-repo clusters score identically under every mode. CLI: --score-mode. Root-config/CLI only; a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (report-level stance, chosen once per run).

optional_blocks.description: Tunables for type-3 / 'optional segment' clone detection — clusters where some members include extra statements not present in others, rendered as default-false bool $include* parameters in the suggested abstraction. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (every sub-knob steers pair/cluster machinery that reads the root config — the old admission carried all five flat values into per-file configs no reader consulted) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

enabled.description: Master switch. When false the containment lens is removed from the pair ladder (sub-Jaccard pairs then reach only the optional IR/ML arms — the bag Jaccard/APTED spine and its size gate are untouched) and AntiUnifier falls back to a single whole-array subtree hole for every divergent stmt array.

containment.description: ContainmentSimilarity threshold for the near-subset fallback used when Jaccard rejects a candidate pair. Higher = stricter.

min_overlap.description: Minimum size ratio (smaller bag mass / larger bag mass) for a near-subset pair to be kept. Prevents pairing a 1-line block with a 100-line one.

max_per_cluster.description: Cap on optional_block holes per cluster before AntiUnifier falls back to a single whole-array hole — guards against pathological seven-boolean signatures.

min_segment_length.description: Minimum stmt-array gap length (in raw stmts) to promote into an optional_block hole — the documented intent. Current truth (2026-11 doc wave): ADMITTED, VALIDATED (>= 1) and BOUND INTO THE CLUSTER-CACHE KEY, but never READ — AntiUnifier stores the value and the LCS promotes unmatched template statements of any length. Until the Refactor-wave leg implements (or retires) it, the default 1 is the only value whose behaviour the docs describe honestly, and changing it invalidates warm cluster caches for identical output (php-dup-finder-once-078 DA-06).

report.description: File-output destinations. Equivalent to --html / --json on the CLI; the SARIF, GitLab SAST, diff, patch, and Checkstyle outputs are CLI-only. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (it names files the run WRITES, so no scanned subtree may choose them (shell-S22 write/ref family posture)) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

html.description: Directory to write the interactive HTML report into.

json.description: Path to write the structured JSON report to.

db_aware.description: ORM-/DB-aware semantic deduplication. When true, the Normalizer runs DbOpCanonicalizer as a pre-pass: recognised database calls across Eloquent, Doctrine, query builders, PDO, mysqli, pg_*, and raw SQL strings rewrite to canonical __DB_<OP>__("table") tokens so equivalent ORM and raw-SQL variants of the same operation cluster together. Two honesty guards ride on it: the generic verbs get/all/save fold only when the receiver chain carries DB evidence (builder table-literal seed, a recognised DB receiver/class name, or an informative user mapping), and SQL-promoted synthetics retain a coarse payload signature — the sorted column set as a structural __DB_COLS_<set> name argument — so same table+verb payloads touching different columns cluster as near-duplicates instead of exact clones. Off by default — enabling it broadens clustering but raises the false-positive ceiling, so it's an explicit opt-in. CLI: --db-aware. Also honored per-subtree: a .phpdup.json carrying true runs the canonical pre-pass for that subtree (once-S67 admit; the value was already a worker-tooling and IndexStore cache-key input, so per-subtree use is cache-safe by construction).

trinity_collapse.description: Trinity-collapse: when true, the Normalizer runs TrinityCollapser as a pre-pass that detects the canonical CRUD trinity (read → mutate → save) and rewrites the three-statement sequence as a single __DB_UPSERT__("entity") synthetic call. Composes with db_aware. Off by default. CLI: --trinity-collapse. Also honored per-subtree (once-S67 admit — same cache-key safety as db_aware).

scorer.description: Scoring tier set. 'default' = stock AST-tier scoring (Jaccard + TED + containment). 'ir' = also enable the IR-tier fallback after AST tiers reject: lift both blocks to canonical IR (Phpdup\Ir\IrLifter) and Jaccard their token bags. Pairs at or above ir_threshold form edges. CLI: --scorer. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (the tier ladder is a pair-level stance chosen once per run; the per-directory admission was inert) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

ir_threshold.description: Multiset-Jaccard threshold for the IR tier. Only consulted when scorer=ir. CLI: --ir-threshold. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (pair-level stance, root reader) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

ml_pair_url.description: External pair-similarity ML sidecar URL. Empty (the default) disables the tier. When set, the very last clustering tier — POSTs a PairFeatures vector to <URL>/score-pair; pairs at or above ml_pair_threshold form edges. http(s) only; SSRF-hardened at admission by SHAPE ONLY — no resolver call happens while the config is validated: canonical IP literals are bit-checked against the refused space (0.0.0.0/8, loopback, RFC 1918, CGNAT, link-local, 192.0.0.0/24, 198.18.0.0/15, multicast/reserved, IPv6 loopback/ULA/link-local/multicast, IPv4-mapped and IPv4-compatible forms, and the NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 well-known prefix's embedded IPv4), file:// / gopher:// and inet_aton numeric shorthands refuse, localhost refuses by name; bare hostnames are grammar-checked and resolved ONCE at dial time, fail-closed there. Returns null on transport failure so unavailability never breaks the run. CLI: --ml-pair-url. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (a sidecar endpoint is a run posture and must never be plantable by a scanned tree (once-S54 make-it-loud, closing the once-076 silent-inert path)) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

ml_pair_threshold.description: Similarity threshold for the ML pair tier. Only consulted when ml_pair_url is set. CLI: --ml-pair-threshold. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (sibling of the URL leg: pair-tier stance, never plantable per-subtree) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

debug_log.description: Path of a file the run appends its debug (very-verbose) pipeline messages to, via Phpdup\Pipeline\DebugLogger — a sink for stage events independent of -v/-vv rendering. Absent (the default) logs nothing to disk. An unwritable path degrades to a surfaced warning and the run still completes (shell-S29 destructor safe-close). Shape rule at load: a non-string or empty string exits 2 ("debug_log must be a non-empty string"). ROOT CONFIG ONLY: it names a file the run WRITES, so a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails discovery loudly (shell-S22 path/ref-bearing family). CLI: --debug-log.

ml_pair_allow_private.description: Opt-in admitting an ml_pair_url sidecar in the PRIVATE address families — loopback, RFC 1918, CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10, link-local, ULA, and their IPv6/embedded (incl. NAT64) spellings — the documented local-sidecar topology (once-S54). Off by default; reserved non-private spaces (0.0.0.0/8, 192.0.0.0/24, 198.18.0.0/15, multicast) stay refused either way. Root-only key: subtree .phpdup.json files carrying it are refused. The root config key takes effect today; the argv spelling does NOT exist at this tip — --ml-pair-allow-private is unregistered in the Command.php option roster (Symfony refuses it as an unknown option, exit 1) and lands with a later option-roster leg. CLI: none in this release (config-file family key until that leg).

llm_url.description: Item 8.2 (`phpdup audit`): generative endpoint BASE for the audit judgment layer. Empty (the default) keeps the LLM pass entirely OFF — `phpdup audit` then ships its audit doc un-annotated with a note, analyze never consults this key, and zero network or cache writes happen anywhere. When set, the audit command POSTs batches of evidence packs to <URL>/annotate (per-finding title/proposal/risk/effort/intentional) and the annotated digest to <URL>/themes (semantic theme labels, summary, landing order); verdicts are cached content-addressed under cache_dir/llm-annotations keyed by host+model+prompt-version+pack-hash so reruns only pay for changed findings, and judgment bytes ONLY are ever stored (never source or packs). http(s) only; SSRF-hardened at admission by SHAPE ONLY — no resolver call during validation (the full ml_pair_url refused-space matrix, re-labelled: reserved spaces stay refused even under llm_allow_private); names resolve fail-closed at dial time. Transport/shape failures degrade to an un-annotated audit at unchanged exit. The bearer token is NOT a config key: it rides ONLY the PHPDUP_LLM_TOKEN environment variable, because reports embed the config section and a key here would leak into shipped artifacts. Read by phpdup audit only; analyze never consumes it. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (the transport endpoint is a run posture, never plantable per-subtree). CLI: none (config-file family key).

llm_model.description: Item 8.2: model name echoed in the audit request body and folded into the annotation cache key, so switching models never replays another model's verdicts. Empty = the endpoint's default model. A non-string fails the load. Read by phpdup audit only; analyze never consumes it. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load. CLI: none (config-file family key).

llm_max_findings.description: Item 8.2: cost cap — the number of top-ranked evidence packs `phpdup audit` sends for annotation (batches of 20); findings beyond it stay un-annotated in the audit doc. The default matches EvidencePackBuilder::TOP_K (100) so the cap binds at the pack ceiling by construction. 0 would silently ship a whole audit with zero verdicts, so the domain starts at 1; values outside 1..1000 fail the load. Read by phpdup audit only; analyze never consumes it. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load. CLI: none (config-file family key).

llm_allow_private.description: Item 8.2: opt-in admitting an llm_url endpoint in the PRIVATE address families (loopback, RFC 1918, CGNAT, link-local, ULA and their IPv6/embedded spellings) — the local sidecar topology, mirrored from ml_pair_allow_private's once-S54 doctrine. Off by default; reserved non-private spaces (0.0.0.0/8, 192.0.0.0/24, 198.18.0.0/15, multicast) stay refused either way. Root-only key: subtree .phpdup.json files carrying it are refused. CLI: none (config-file family key; no argv spelling exists). Read by phpdup audit only; analyze never consumes it.

db_symbols.description: User-extensible DB symbol equivalence registry. Custom method/function name → canonical-op mappings merged on top of the stock DbOpRegistry entries. Also honored per-subtree: a .phpdup.json's buckets APPEND to the root map for that subtree (once-S67). Keys are matched case-insensitively (both stored keys and looked-up call names are lower-cased), so the lower-case convention and camelCase pack keys both work; values are one of db.read | db.write | db.delete | db.execute | db.query. Profiles ship symbol packs (db-aware-laravel, db-aware-doctrine, db-aware-cake) that can be loaded via --profile.

methods.description: Method-name → canonical-op map. Matches against StaticCall, MethodCall, and NullsafeMethodCall names regardless of receiver; name matching is case-insensitive (camelCase keys fold to the same entry as lower-case). Exempt from the receiver-evidence gate only when the mapped op differs from the stock classification of a generic tier name (get/all/save) — a verbatim re-statement keeps the gate (engine-003).

functions.description: Function-name → canonical-op map. Matches against FuncCall names; name matching is case-insensitive (camelCase keys fold to the same entry as lower-case). Not subject to the receiver-evidence gate.

drift_flags.description: Item 4.1: vocabulary arming the DriftAnalyzer's drift predicates over a cluster's members (guard/sanitizer/auth/literal/option divergence between clones). Precedence: CLI dict > this file > the --profile tier (profiles generic and db-aware-myadmin ship a block); a layer that names the block replaces it wholesale. Empty/absent = the analyzer is INERT and reports are byte-unchanged — no-profile runs (incl. Golden and the CI legs) never arm it. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — a subtree choosing which drift findings exist is the same suppression-hazard family as 'accepted' (item 4.4). Arming without the key: --profile generic|auto.

_description.description: Profiles ship a nested human note; the loader accepts and strips it.

predicates.description: Enabled predicate codes (DriftAnalyzer::PREDICATE_*). Any other entry is refused with the allowed list. The block arms only what is enumerated; omit for an inert vocabulary.

sanitizers.description: Lower-cased call names classified as sanitizing (the sanitizer-divergence arm compares descriptors' callNames lower-cased). Entry names must be non-empty strings.

auth.description: Lower-cased call names classified as auth checks (guards an auth-missing drift; snake_case convention — matching is case-folded).

options.description: Security-relevant option CONSTANTS, verbatim spelling (e.g. CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER). SCOPES the option-divergence arm: it fires only when the divergent argument position's resolved name is enumerated here (§4.1 letter; r1 m-2). Unresolvable or off-list names earn no claim.

low_memory.description: Reduce memory footprint: use CompactNgramBag — bags keyed by a masked-positive 63-bit int derived from the xxh64 hex digest as (hi&0x7FFFFFFF)<<32|lo, not a 32-bit fingerprint (the old phrasing; engine-S18b era truth) — plus CanonicalNodePool interning. Off by default; hex bags remain the default species (the flip is gated by FingerprintModeAcceptanceTest). CLI: --low-memory. Also honored per-subtree: a .phpdup.json carrying true swaps that subtree's bags to the compact form (the flag rides the worker tooling key).

fail_on_impact.description: CI gate: exit code 3 when total cluster impact exceeds this value. 0 = disabled. CLI: --fail-on-impact. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (it gates the one final report; the old per-directory admission was inert) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

max_clusters.description: CI gate: exit code 3 when cluster count exceeds this value. 0 = disabled. CLI: --max-clusters. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (it gates the one final report) (once-S67, php-dup-finder-once-077: admitted-but-inert keys are a lie the loader no longer tells).

baseline.description: CI baseline file for incremental duplication gating and the accepted-decision register. If file exists: load baseline and exit 4 if new clusters are found (clusters whose member content hashes are not all present in some baseline cluster). If file does not exist: write baseline snapshot and exit 0 (first-run auto-baseline). The file may also carry a top-level 'dispositions' map (v4) of finding_id -> {status: accepted|unresolved, provenance, timestamp}: accepted findings drop out of the main report into a baseline appendix, unresolved ones are triage markers only, and an accepted finding whose content resurfaces under a new id re-enters the report fail-open and is annotated resurfaced. CLI: --baseline. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — it names a file the run reads and writes, so no scanned subtree may choose it (shell-S22).

baseline_out.description: Write current clusters as a baseline snapshot to FILE (overwrites existing). Useful for explicitly creating or updating baselines. CLI: --baseline-out. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — it names a file phpdup OVERWRITES, so no scanned subtree may choose it (shell-S22).

diff_base.description: Git ref for diff-scoped analysis. When set, phpdup scans only files changed in `git diff --name-only <ref>..HEAD` plus their clone cohort (files sharing n-gram fingerprints with the changed files). Useful for per-PR analysis in CI. CLI: --diff-base. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — the ref becomes argv of an external git call, so no scanned subtree may choose it (shell-S22; argv confinement of the ref itself lands shell-S23/output-S52).

apply.description: Enable the report pipeline's apply mode: a cumulative apply.diff of every cluster refactor patch is written under refactored/ (dry-run posture — the preview apply.diff carries the same text --patch emits; real file rewrites happen with --dry-run=false). Effective value is flag OR config file: --apply turns it on from argv, "apply": true in the root config activates the same mode with no flag, and the flag wins a disagreement (it arrives as a CLI override, which outranks the file layer). Shape-checked like every other key — a non-boolean value exits 2 from --validate-config and from a run. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load (once-S67: the loud refusal replaces the old silent ignore — apply arms real source rewrites, so no scanned subtree may choose it; sibling of the shell-S22 write/ref family). CLI: --apply.

accepted.description: Item 4.4 (the APPLY half): stable finding ids the team has explicitly ACCEPTED as kept duplication. Matching is exact finding_id equality; accepted findings drop out of the main report and are enumerated in a baseline appendix (CLI trailer + HTML section), never silently. Acceptance sources in precedence order: the --baseline file's 'dispositions' map (registry, with provenance), harvested @phpdup-ignore directives (code-local, file-verified), then this list (project-wide). Accepted entries that RESURFACE after content drift re-enter the report fail-open for re-review and are annotated resurfaced in the appendix. ROOT CONFIG ONLY: a per-directory .phpdup.json carrying this key fails the load — a suppression register is a decision surface, and the discovery walk lets any scanned subtree plant one (same posture as the shell-S22 path/ref family; item 4.4).
